notes:
## New features
- Rotate buildings and area sources. Selecting one shows a rotate grip above it; drag to rotate about its centre, and hold Shift to snap to the drawing angle increment (15° by default, set in Preferences). Holes and facade receptors rotate with the building, and each rotation is a single undo step.
- The Contours editor shows the sheet area as a faint dashed frame. Locking the view fixes the frame in place while you keep panning and zooming. Double-click the frame to adjust its corners; the sheet's proportions are kept.
- Recent contour runs are listed under the sheet selector for one-click loading, named by scenario and time slice. Renaming a scenario relabels its runs. Runs from a deleted scenario keep its last name, marked deleted and stale. History still holds the full list.
- Minor isolines for SmartSmooth contours: set the interval (default 1 dB) and width (default 75% of the outline). They use the band colours, carry no labels and stop at screening edges.
- Band-label controls: font size (6–14 pt) and labels per line (up to 1–6). Short lines, such as small rings near a source, get fewer labels or none.
- Projects from earlier versions of AURIS are upgraded when opened. A notice lists what changed, and the project is marked unsaved so the upgraded version can be saved over the old file.

## Changes
- Interpolated Raster shows the calculated grid at the chosen detail (2×, 4×, …) as finer cells, sampled from the screening-aware field, so shadow boundaries stay sharp and straight rather than stair-stepped.
- Stronger simplification at the upper levels. Extreme may now move a level contour by up to two grid spacings, or 1 dB from the calculated field, which removes grid-scale notches. Screening shadow boundaries keep their original tight limit, so Bézier smoothing still curves them.
- Labelled isolines are drawn from the band edges themselves, so lines and fills always coincide.
- Projects that used the pre-2024 ground method now use the ISO 9613-2:2024 General method (Clause 7.3.1, including the Formula (11) geometry correction). Results may change slightly; recalculate before reporting.
- Contour sheets that used earlier SmartSmooth predecessors (Smooth, Engineering Linear, Adaptive Linear) now use SmartSmooth and keep their settings.
- Saved projects record the AURIS version that saved them.
- Calculations run at a lower priority than the interface, so editing and navigation stay responsive during long runs.
- The packaged app keeps compiled QML and GPU pipelines between launches, so the 3D view opens faster after the first time.
- The splash's moving gradient is more visible, and its release line reads "Release 0.12.0". The autosave recovery dialog and colour band strip are refreshed, and the palette summary is now one line with the full calculation basis in its tooltip.
- ISO 9613-2:2024 reflections (Clause 7.5) are checked by automated tests against an independent reference: single walls, parallel walls up to the chosen order, the reflector size criterion, and equality between contour and receptor results.

## Bug fixes
- Panning and zooming the Sheet preview no longer lags. The map moves immediately and re-renders once you stop.
- Band labels sit on their isoline with a clean gap, instead of appearing crossed out or beside the line on map-sized projects.
- Changing minor isolines, label size or labels per line now updates the contours immediately.
- In the level band list, the last band no longer overlaps the Add band and Remove buttons.
- The Editor no longer becomes laggy while receptor results are calculating.
- Interpolated views no longer fail with "TopologyException: side location conflict" where contour rings touch.
- Screening shadow boundaries no longer show a dashed seam of missing cells in Interpolated Raster.
- A failure while preparing the interpolation field now shows its fallback message instead of an internal error.
- Calculation workers no longer receive a copy of the organisation logo and consultant directory.
